title: Finite relations and Fitting generators for split tensor quotients
statement:
Let $A,C,B$ be commutative rings with homomorphisms $A\to C$ and $A\to B$. Fix an $A$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $C$, where $d\ge0$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Set $T=C\otimes_A B$, with its $B$-algebra structure through the second factor [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property]. Let $D$ be a commutative $B$-algebra and let $\theta:T\xrightarrow{\sim}B\times D$ be a $B$-algebra isomorphism. Let $K=(k_1,\ldots,k_r)\subset C$ be an ideal generated by the displayed finite list, where $r\ge0$. Let $J\subset T$ be generated by $k\otimes1$ for $k\in K$, and let $H\subset D$ be generated by $\operatorname{pr}_2\theta(k\otimes1)$ for $k\in K$. Put $v_i=e_i\otimes1$, $\varepsilon=\theta^{-1}(1,0)$ and $w_{ji}=(k_j\otimes1)v_i$. Let $q_A:C\twoheadrightarrow C/K$ be the quotient map and $q_B:T\twoheadrightarrow D/H$ the composite of $\operatorname{pr}_2\theta$ with the quotient map. Then
$$\ker(q_A)=\operatorname{span}_A\{k_j e_i\}_{j,i},\quad J=\operatorname{span}_B\{w_{ji}\}_{j,i},\quad \ker(q_B)=B\varepsilon+J=\operatorname{span}_B(\{\varepsilon\}\cup\{w_{ji}\}_{j,i}).$$
In particular $C/K$ is a finitely presented $A$-module and $D/H$ is a finitely presented $B$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. Write $I_0(P)$ for the presentation-independent zeroth kernel-minor ideal of a finite module $P$ [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change]. The ideal $I_0(C/K)\subset A$ is generated by determinants of all ordered $d$-tuples of the coordinate vectors of $k_je_i$ in the basis $(e_i)$; the ideal $I_0(D/H)\subset B$ is generated by determinants of all ordered $d$-tuples of the coordinate vectors of $\varepsilon,w_{ji}$ in the scalar-extended basis $(v_i)$ [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Repetitions in tuples are allowed. For $d=0$ the single empty determinant is $1$. Thus both ideals are finitely generated. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0812 (lemma-trick-fitting-ideal), finite-generation assertion, expanded into finite relation lists for the two quotient modules; literature/stacks-project/more-algebra.tex, Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics), proof of (4), and Tag 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal), kernel-row description.

proof.text: Define $f:C\to B$ by $f(c)=\operatorname{pr}_1\theta(c\otimes1)$. The tensor algebra maps in [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] and $B$-linearity of $\theta$ give $f(a\cdot1_C)=a\cdot1_B$ and $\operatorname{pr}_1\theta(c\otimes b)=bf(c)$. Thus $f$ is an $A$-algebra homomorphism satisfying the extra hypothesis of [lem-trf-split-tensor-quotient-decomposition]. That lemma gives the $B$-basis $(v_i)$ and $\theta(J)=KB\times H$, where $KB$ is generated by $f(K)$.

source.place: Tag 0812 (lemma-trick-fitting-ideal), product splitting and its quotient ideals.

proof.text: The quotient map has kernel $K$ by [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Every $k\in K$ has the form $\sum_j c_jk_j$. Expand $c_j=\sum_i a_{ji}e_i$ using [def-weil-pbc-free-module]; then $k=\sum_{j,i}a_{ji}k_je_i$. Conversely every $k_je_i$ lies in $K$. Hence $\ker(q_A)=\operatorname{span}_A\{k_je_i\}$.

source.place: Tag 0812 (lemma-trick-fitting-ideal), finite-generation assertion: explicit relations for C/K.

proof.text: Write $s_j=k_j\otimes1$. For $k=\sum_j c_jk_j$, the tensor algebra identities [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] give $k\otimes1=\sum_j(c_j\otimes1)s_j$. Thus $J=(s_1,\ldots,s_r)$ as an ideal. Every $t\in J$ is $\sum_j t_js_j$; expanding $t_j=\sum_i b_{ji}v_i$ in the basis from Step 1 gives $t=\sum_{j,i}b_{ji}w_{ji}$. The reverse containment holds because $w_{ji}=s_jv_i\in J$. Therefore $J=\operatorname{span}_B\{w_{ji}\}$.

source.place: Tag 0812 (lemma-trick-fitting-ideal), finite-generation assertion: relations in the scalar-extended algebra.

proof.text: By the quotient description [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], $q_B(t)=0$ exactly when $\theta(t)=(b,h)$ with $h\in H$. By $\theta(J)=KB\times H$ from [lem-trf-split-tensor-quotient-decomposition], choose $j\in J$ with $\theta(j)=(0,h)$. Since $\theta(b\varepsilon)=(b,0)$, one has $t=b\varepsilon+j$. Conversely $q_B$ kills both $\varepsilon$ and $J$. This proves $\ker(q_B)=B\varepsilon+J$ and, by Step 3, the asserted finite span. The map $q_B$ is surjective: lift any class in $D/H$ to $h\in D$ and use $\theta^{-1}(0,h)$.

source.place: Tag 0812 (lemma-trick-fitting-ideal), complementary quotient; the kernel is written explicitly.

proof.text: In coordinates for $(e_i)$ and $(v_i)$ the maps $q_A,q_B$ therefore give exact sequences $A^{rd}\to A^d\to C/K\to0$ and $B^{1+rd}\to B^d\to D/H\to0$. The first arrows send standard basis vectors to the coordinates of $k_je_i$ and, respectively, $\varepsilon,w_{ji}$; their images are exactly the kernels computed above. Surjectivity also shows both quotients are generated by the $d$ displayed basis images. These finite exact sequences are finite presentations by [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], compute $I_0$ using these rank-$d$ surjections. For $d>0$, its generators are determinants of $d$ arbitrary kernel rows. For either finite relation list $(u_\alpha)$, write row $z_\ell=\sum_\alpha a_{\ell\alpha}u_\alpha$. Distributing the finite products in the permutation formula [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] gives
$$\det(z_1,\ldots,z_d)=\sum_{\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d}\left(\prod_{\ell=1}^d a_{\ell\alpha_\ell}\right)\det(u_{\alpha_1},\ldots,u_{\alpha_d}).$$
Consequently all kernel determinants belong to the ideal generated by the displayed ordered-tuple determinants. Conversely each displayed tuple consists of kernel rows, so its determinant belongs to $I_0$. Applying this to both lists proves the two ideal descriptions, allowing repeated indices.

source.place: Tag 07Z8 (lemma-fitting-ideal), kernel-row description; Tag 07ZA (lemma-fitting-ideal-basics), proof of (4).

proof.text: The two finite relation lists have $rd$ and $1+rd$ entries. For fixed $d>0$ their ordered $d$-tuples form finite sets, so Step 6 gives finite ideal generating sets, even when a list is empty. For $d=0$, both quotient modules are zero since they are quotients of rank-zero modules. Their zeroth kernel-minor ideals are the unit ideals by [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-independence-base-change], and the sole empty tuple has determinant $1$ by [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Thus the same descriptions hold. No argument used a Noetherian hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem splitTensorQuotient_finite_fitting {A : Type u} {C : Type v} {B : Type w} {D : Type z} [CommRing A] [CommRing C] [CommRing B] [CommRing D] [Algebra A C] [Algebra A B] [Algebra B D] {d r : ℕ} (e : Module.Basis (Fin d) A C) (K : Ideal C) (k : Fin r → C) (hK : K = Ideal.span (Set.range k)) : @_root_.id (∀ [Algebra B (C ⊗[A] B)], Prop) (fun [Algebra B (C ⊗[A] B)] ↦ ∀ θ : C ⊗[A] B ≃ₐ[B] B × D, Function.Surjective (splitComplementQuotient θ.toRingEquiv K) ∧ LinearMap.ker (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A K).toLinearMap = Submodule.span A (Set.range (fun a : Fin r × Fin d ↦ k a.1 * e a.2)) ∧ (Ideal.map (includeLeftRingHom : C →+* C ⊗[A] B) K).restrictScalars B = Submodule.span B (Set.range (splitTensorRelations e k)) ∧ (RingHom.ker (splitComplementQuotient θ.toRingEquiv K)).restrictScalars B = Submodule.span B {θ.symm (1, 0)} ⊔ (Ideal.map (includeLeftRingHom : C →+* C ⊗[A] B) K).restrictScalars B ∧ (RingHom.ker (splitComplementQuotient θ.toRingEquiv K)).restrictScalars B = Submodule.span B (Set.range (splitComplementRelations θ.toRingEquiv e k)) ∧ Module.FinitePresentation A (C ⧸ K) ∧ Module.FinitePresentation B (D ⧸ splitComplementIdeal θ.toRingEquiv K) ∧ LinearMap.presentationFittingIdeal ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A K).toLinearMap.comp e.equivFun.symm.toLinearMap) 0 = Ideal.span (Set.range (fun t : Fin d → Fin r × Fin d ↦ Matrix.det (fun i l ↦ e.repr (k (t i).1 * e (t i).2) l))) ∧ (splitComplementPresentation θ.toRingEquiv e K).presentationFittingIdeal 0 = Ideal.span (Set.range (fun t : Fin d → Option (Fin r × Fin d) ↦ Matrix.det (fun i l ↦ (e.baseChange B).repr (_root_.TensorProduct.comm A C B (splitComplementRelations θ.toRingEquiv e k (t i))) l))) ∧ (LinearMap.presentationFittingIdeal ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ A K).toLinearMap.comp e.equivFun.symm.toLinearMap) 0).FG ∧ ((splitComplementPresentation θ.toRingEquiv e K).presentationFittingIdeal 0).FG) (rightAlgebra (R := A) (A := C) (B := B))
